claims.text: 403 means the server understood the request but refuses it (RFC 9110 15.5.4; a client may retry with different credentials). For an ownership refusal, a new token for the same customer carries the same sub, so it gets the same answer.

In ASP.NET Core, authentication runs in middleware on every request. Some authorization, like [Authorize], needs only the caller; an ownership check needs the resource, so it is made per endpoint after the resource is loaded.
Filtering a query by the caller's id, as List does, is one way to enforce ownership: data the caller does not own is never fetched.
A request that fails authentication gets 401 only on an endpoint marked [Authorize]: live, a malformed token got 401 from GET /api/v1/orders but 200 from GET /api/v1/orders/3.
